success_patterns: Hub identification by single edits: in the operator-equation item, every other option was one edit from the winner (ε^O halved vs not, ε^I halved vs not, sum over l≥1 vs odd l, 'at most one' vs 'only one'). In the homogeneous-solution item, the winner was the hub of a ladder with extras and truncations around it. Marking the isolated edit in each distractor and choosing the hub settled these items.

Quantifier order and scope were checked literally against the stem. In the Diophantine-approximation item, 'for every N there exist b for every β' is a swapped order, 'sufficiently large N' shrinks the stem's N≥2, and a constant independent of ε is an over-claim. The winner kept C_{d,k,ε}, all N≥2, and all β exactly as the stem says.

The stem's parameter range was respected exactly. In the Hölder item, extending to 1/κ or to the closed endpoint was rejected, 'every neighborhood' was rejected, and the plain neighborhood form was chosen. The C_β form was treated as a weaker hedge, since shrinking the neighborhood absorbs the constant.

Two-sided bounds were required to use the same function in the lower and upper estimate (the Brownian-motion item). Mismatched exponents (1/2 vs 1, 3/2 vs 1), a different scale (1/|log ε|), and one-sided bounds were all discarded.

Single-clause swaps in equivalence statements were caught. The ambient set was changed from D to D_{Y∪Y'}, equality was weakened to ⊆, an iff was reduced to one-way implications, and 'decides' was inflated to 'produces explicit witnesses'. The plain iff with a 'decides' clause won.

The 'strongest' item was resolved at the pivot between true-but-weaker (finitely many; mere positivity; no explicit rate) and sharper-but-unjustified (6g-6 instead of 6g, 'even without the hypothesis', an unconditional two-sided estimate, an invented constant). The winner used all of the stem's hypotheses and added nothing unprovable.

Numerical options were recomputed from the closed form (log_τ 2 /4 ≈ 0.1966, /3 ≈ 0.262, log_2 τ /4 ≈ 0.318). A divisor-constant or log-base swap was treated as a single-edit corruption rather than echoed from the stem.

patch.reasoning: All 8 trajectories were correct, and each winning move is already stated in the skill: the clause split, hub and odd-one-out test, quantifier-order and range checks, matching two-sided rates, the pivot rung of the strength ladder, and the PRIORITY PROCEDURE filters. The previous step's restructure (a new STEP 0 table plus a deletion) was rejected, and it coincided with a drop on strength-mismatch items. Adding or rewording rules now risks that regression and would only restate existing rules without changing the persistent structural failures. So no edits are proposed; the current text should be kept intact to protect these stable successes.
